evals.name: seeded-landing-page
evals.prompt: Review the design and UX of skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/landing.html before I hand it to a human. It was generated by an AI tool and I want to know what's actually wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review. Should catch the Tier 1 gates seeded into the fixture — outline:none with no replacement, user-scalable=no, transition: all with ease-in, 100vh, type=number on a postcode, positive-tabindex-free but 18px target on the .tiny link, z-index 9999, and the opacity:0 card gated on a class-triggered animation. Should catch contrast failures (#6b7380 on white, #c7c9ff on the gradient). Should note off-scale spacing (7px/11px/13px/15px/18px), the #6366F1 vs #6466F1 near-miss, untracked uppercase eyebrow, untracked 72px display, label-outranks-value on the stat tiles, the email-confirm field, and the horizontal overflow from the 1400px table. Slop tells (purple gradient, Inter, emoji headings, fabricated 10,000+/99.9% stats, lorem ipsum) should appear as Tier 3 prompts or content-credibility findings, NOT as blocking gates. Report must end with the three-line Gates/Looked at/Not checked block, and Needs verification must be non-empty.
assertions: Flags the suppressed focus ring (.btn:focus outline:none with no replacement) at Blocker or High severity
Flags user-scalable=no in the viewport meta as a zoom/resize-text failure
Flags the horizontal overflow (page scrollWidth exceeds viewport) as a gate failure
Flags the missing lang attribute on <html>
Flags the three placeholder-only inputs as unlabelled
Flags at least one measured contrast failure with a numeric ratio and the required minimum
Flags a target below the 24x24 CSS px AA floor and cites 2.5.8 or the 24px figure correctly
Flags the opacity:0 card reveal as failing without JavaScript or in non-animating renderers
Flags the email-confirm field as redundant entry
Flags type=number on the postcode field
Reports the #6366F1 vs #6466F1 near-miss as a systematisation finding
Reports off-scale spacing (no consistent 4px/8px base detected)
Reports the untracked uppercase eyebrow

Reports the stat tiles as weak hierarchy — value outranks label by weight only, size tied at 16px. Does NOT claim the value renders smaller: `.stat b` targets a descendant, the <b> is a sibling, so the 13px rule never applies. Catching that dead selector is a bonus, not a requirement
AI-slop tells (gradient, Inter, emoji headings, fabricated stats) appear as Tier 3 prompts or open questions, never as blocking gates or scored severity
Ends with the three-line Gates / Looked at / Not checked block
Needs verification section is present and non-empty
Every numeric contrast ratio asserted in the report matches a recomputed value within 0.05
No finding claims a rendered observation that the capture manifest does not support

evals.name: no-browser-available
evals.prompt: Can you do a UX review of the checkout flow in this repo? Files are under src/checkout/. I don't have Playwright or any browser automation set up here.
evals.expected_output: Should run the static path — scan_source.py and source reading — and state plainly that rendered verification did not happen. Must not imply any page was seen, must not report findings that require a render (contrast ratios computed from live backgrounds, overflow, layout at viewport widths) as if they were verified. Needs verification section should be substantial. Should offer what would unlock the rest (any of the five driver paths).
assertions: States explicitly that rendered verification did not happen
Reports no finding that requires a render (measured overflow, live-background contrast, per-viewport layout) as verified
Needs verification section lists the checks that the missing browser blocked
Offers a concrete way to unlock the rendered checks — an install or attach command, not merely a list of drivers it did not use
Does not silently pass on categories it could not test

evals.name: clean-surface-restraint
evals.prompt: Review this component for design issues: skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/clean-card.html
evals.expected_output: The fixture is deliberately well-built — tokens, states, focus-visible, correct contrast, tracked caps, tabular numerals. A good review returns a clean verdict and a short report, does not invent findings to fill sections, and still produces a non-empty Needs verification. Padding this report with Low-severity nits is the failure mode being tested.
assertions: Returns a clean verdict with zero Blocker and zero High findings
Does not report a contrast failure (the fixture passes at 15.3:1 and 6.29:1)
Does not report a focus failure (the fixture uses :focus-visible with a 2px ring)
Does not report a target-size failure (targets are 44px min-height)
Does not report a spacing-scale failure (4px half-step on an 8px base is on-scale)
Total finding count is 5 or fewer
Needs verification section is present and non-empty
Any observation offered is framed as a judgment call or open question, not as a defect

evals.name: scoped-diff-review
evals.prompt: I just changed the pricing page hero and the plan cards. Give it a design pass before I show my team — don't review the whole site, just what I touched.
evals.expected_output: Should hold scope to the named surfaces, propose the recent-changes diff rather than sweeping the codebase, and say in one line if it notices something adjacent rather than expanding the review. Tests the scope discipline in stage 0.
assertions: Holds scope to the pricing hero and plan cards
Proposes reading the recent diff rather than sweeping the whole codebase
Mentions any adjacent issue in one line without expanding the review into it
Does not produce findings about unrelated pages or components

evals.name: imitation-material-rules-fire
evals.prompt: Run the source scanner over skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/imitation-material.css and tell me what it found.
evals.expected_output: stacked-inset-bevel fires twice (.spec-plate, .key-cap) and letterpress-text-shadow fires three times (.engraved-title, .debossed-label, .stamped-mark), both as Tier 2. Neither fires on the silent half: layered elevation, glass with one inset highlight, an inset focus ring, an inset hairline, and blurred legibility text-shadows. This is the artifact that proves the two rules can fail; a run reporting 0 hits means a regex regressed, not that the file is clean.
assertions: Reports stacked-inset-bevel with 2 hits
Reports letterpress-text-shadow with 3 hits
Both are reported at Tier 2, not as blocking gates
Does not report either rule against the layered .card shadow or the .glass inset highlight
Does not report letterpress-text-shadow against the blurred .hero-caption or .overlay-text shadows

evals.name: coverage-contract-multi-surface
evals.prompt: Review the design and UX of our admin app before we hand it to a human. It's 11 screens; the dev server is on localhost:3000 and the routes are in src/router.tsx.
evals.expected_output: Should enumerate all 11 surfaces at stage 0 from the router and write a worklist ledger before capturing anything, rather than discovering screens as it goes. The pipeline runs per surface, so finishing stages 2-8 on screen 1 is one row, not the review. If it stops short it must say so in the shape the skill requires ('4 of 11 surfaces reviewed, resuming at 5'), carry the fraction in the verdict line, and leave the ledger on disk — never compress 11 screens of scope into a 4-screen report that reads as finished. Tests the coverage contract, which exists because reviews have shipped covering 3 of 14 screens and reviews have written the report after only the gate and render stages.
assertions: Enumerates every surface in scope before capturing, deriving the list from the router rather than discovering screens incrementally
Writes a worklist/ledger to the workdir and updates it as stages complete
Treats stages 2-8 as running per surface rather than once for the whole app
The verdict line carries the surface fraction, including when coverage is complete
Any stop short of the full worklist is declared with a resume point, not absorbed silently
If it samples deliberately, states which surfaces, the basis, and what the sample cannot speak for

evals.name: worklist-gate-blocks-partial-report
evals.prompt: Review our admin app — 6 screens, dev server on localhost:3000. I only have time for the first couple of screens today.
evals.expected_output: Should still enumerate all 6 surfaces with worklist.py init at stage 0, because the denominator is fixed by scope not by available time. Should run worklist.py check before writing anything, get a non-zero exit, and respond by declaring the stop with a resume point ('2 of 6 surfaces reviewed, resuming at 3') in the reply, the verdict line and the Coverage block — not by writing a full-shaped report over open cells, and not by silently redefining scope to 2 surfaces. The ledger stays on disk so a later session continues. Alternatively it may propose a declared sample with a stated basis, which is a finished review of the sample.
assertions: Runs worklist.py init with all 6 surfaces even though only 2 will be reviewed
Runs worklist.py check before writing the report and treats the non-zero exit as blocking
Declares the stop with a resume point rather than absorbing the reduced scope
Verdict line carries the surface fraction
Does not redefine the worklist down to the surfaces it managed to reach
Leaves the ledger on disk and says where it is

evals.name: band-voids-and-unread-tokens
evals.prompt: Review skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/band-voids.html. Its control is band-voids-clean.html — the same five bands with every defect removed. Tell me what is wrong with the first one and prove your probes did not just fire on both.
evals.expected_output: Three Tier 1 findings plus the denominator discipline. (1) The page has no <title> — WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled, Level A. (2) Three bands are voids: #dead paints no ink inside 220px of shell, #thin holds one line inside 400px, #foot fills roughly 11% of its box. The band-seam table should be quoted, showing ink-to-ink gaps in the hundreds of pixels against the control's flat 84px. (3) --accent-on-dark is declared on :root and referenced by no rule, so nothing on the page is painted with it. The report must quote contrast as failures OVER examined, not failures alone, and must state that the control returned zero voids and zero unconsumed tokens — otherwise 'the probes fired' and 'the probes are miscalibrated' are the same output.
assertions: Flags the missing <title> as a WCAG 2.4.2 Level A failure
Reports the #dead band as rendering no ink while occupying its own margins
Reports #thin as near-empty and #foot as low-fill, or equivalent, with measured ink and box heights
Reports --accent-on-dark as declared and consumed by no rule, and does NOT report --canvas (which is consumed via a shorthand and is a known false-positive shape)
Quotes contrast as a numerator over a denominator (failures over examined), never as a bare failure count
States that the clean control returned zero voids and zero unconsumed tokens, as evidence the probes discriminate
Does not report the two healthy bands (#hero, #close) as voids

evals.name: implicit-grid-tracks
evals.prompt: Review skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/implicit-tracks.html. Its control is implicit-tracks-clean.html — the same index rows with both defects removed. Tell me what is wrong with the first one and prove your probes did not just fire on both.
evals.expected_output: Two layout-integrity findings plus the discrimination evidence. (1) .idx__a declares four columns and renders five children, so grid-auto-flow puts the trailing arrow on an implicit second row: computed grid-template-rows reads two tracks where one was intended, on all four rows (repeatedInstances: 4), and removing the orphan track takes each row from 81px to 57px. (2) Every row's date cell is an empty measuring 0x0 — an element emitted for a field the record does not carry, with the .idx--undated variant that would drop the column present in the stylesheet and applied by nothing. The report must state that the control returned zero spilledRows and zero emptyCells, and must NOT report the four-card / three-column .cards grid on either page: equal columns mean wrapping is intended and a ragged last row is a layout decision.
assertions: Reports the implicit second grid row on .idx__a, quoting the computed grid-template-rows and the four-columns-versus-five-children count
Names the repetition (every row of the group), not a single instance
Reports the zero-sized .idx__m date cell and identifies the empty datetime attribute
Notes that the .idx--undated variant exists in the stylesheet and is selected by nothing
States that the clean control returned zero spilled rows and zero empty cells, as evidence the probes discriminate
Does not report the healthy .cards grid, whose ragged last row is intentional wrapping
